dedupe_keys.name: soil foundation structure interaction effects on the cyclic failure potential of silts and clays

description: Soil-Foundation-Structure Interaction Effects on the Cyclic Failure Potential of Silts and Clays is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Scott Brandenberg, University of California Los Angeles (ucla.edu). Earthquake-induced ground failure has resulted in billions of dollars of damage during recent earthquakes. Soils can be broadly characterized as exhibiting either "sand-like" or "clay-like" behavior with respect to strength loss during earthquakes. This project focuses on cyclic failure of "clay-like" soils, which are less well understood than "sand-like" soils. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-db7h-t150. Keywords: Cyclic Softening, Fine-Grained Soil, Soil-Foundation-Structure Interaction. Published 2020-09-30. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
